
A rule is the unit an agent reads, writes and supersedes, so every normative statement in the corpus is the text of a rule version. A spec holds no normative text of its own. It is a **template**: a title, template text the spec owns, and an arrangement, an ordered list of entries, each with a position and a depth. Section numbers and anchors are derived from it (WL-REQ-165). An entry is either a rule or a spec heading. Template text is prose and markup between entries that decides nothing (WL-REQ-1367): overviews, motivation, non-goals, deferral and "designed, not built" pointers, plan indexes, open questions, a glossary's table of terms. It renders in place, carries no ref, no versions of its own and no edges, and is versioned with the arrangement (WL-SPEC-77#sec-3a). A reader gets the spec end to end; only the entries are rows.

Plans, minutes and notes contain no rules and keep a stored body.
